The ALE (Address Latch Enable) signal in the Intel 8085 microprocessor is used to latch the lower 8 bits of the address (A0–A7) from the multiplexed address/data bus (AD0–AD7) into an external latch.  
When ALE is high, the AD0–AD7 lines carry the lower address bits; when ALE goes low, those bits are latched externally, and the same lines then act as the data bus.  

- (A) is incorrect because ALE being high doesn’t enable the data bus — it enables the address latch to capture the low-order address.  
- (B) is incorrect because ALE high does not latch data; it latches the address.  
- (C) is incorrect because ALE high does not disable the data bus — the data bus is simply not being used for data at that moment.  
- (D) is incorrect because not all listed functions are true.  

The correct function of ALE high is to allow the low-order address to be placed on the bus so it can be latched externally.  

Final answer: (A)
